messages:
sofia: Heads-up — AcmeCorp (dedicated pool us-west-2) reporting a sudden spike of 429s starting ~15:42 UTC. Customer says requests used to be fine; started after a config push yesterday.

mike: @sofia can you grab a sample request id? any error payloads?

sofia: sample req id: rq_20260317_akl9f. Error body is 429 with message: "rate limit exceeded". No 5xx. Customer timeline: big batch job + normal traffic. They expected autoscale to handle burst.

jamal: ok checking quota service logs for tenant acmecorp... grabbing link: https://internal/redwood/quotas/acmecorp - looks like per-tenant unit cap set to 60000 but units documentation expects "units per minute" vs runtime treating as "units per second" in the Dedicated config. :eyes:

quota-bot: [automated] tenant acmecorp quota last-modified by support@acme on 2026-03-16T22:10:01Z, change: units=60000, window=1, window_unit=second

mike: if that's true then 60k/sec is huge, but runtime reads window_unit differently? is the Dedicated rate adaptor using milliseconds somewhere?

jamal: digging — runtime codepath at serving/rate_limiter/tenant_quota.go shows the conversion: if window_unit == "minute" then divide by 60 else if "second" use value directly. But the UI previously sent window_unit as empty string on legacy edits, yielding default of "minute" in UI but backlog-sync job writes it as "second". So mismatch.

sofia: so customer saw throttles because the quota was interpreted as much smaller than they expected?

jamal: exactly. The change that support pushed used the legacy UI, which left window_unit blank. The sync job later normalized to "second" and reduced effective rate by factor 60. That explains sudden 429s after the sync ran.

mike: we need an immediate mitigations: 1) bump tenant quota to previous effective rate as emergency, 2) pause quota-sync-job for the tenant so it doesn't flip again, 3) investigate UI+sync fix. I can push a hotfix to the sync job later today.

sofia: I've asked Acme for consent to temporarily increase quota. They approved via support ticket #5319.

deploy-bot: [deploy] starting roll for service: quota-sync (canary) — trace: d4f2c.

mike: hold on the full rollout. Jamal, can you patch the sync job to preserve explicitly-empty window_unit as "minute" for legacy edits? Also add a check: if normalized change would reduce effective rate by >5x, create a require-confirmation alert.

jamal: yes patching now. Quick patch diff: 
```
- if window_unit == "" { window_unit = "second" }
+ if window_unit == "" { window_unit = legacyDefault() } // preserves previous semantics
```
I'll open PR and request quick review.

sofia: I've updated Acme's quota to 3_600_000 units/min (matches pre-sync effective). Monitoring shows 429s dropping to near zero.

mike: good. Follow-ups: - eng-runtime to add a metric for "quota-normalization-impact" - product to update UI copy so it's explicit about units - support runbook to include quick-check steps for quota-sync. I'll file tickets.

sofia: thanks team. I'll confirm with Acme after 1h and close the support case if stable. :thumbsup:

jamal: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/quota-sync/pulls/298 — included alert and unit-preserve change.

mike: leaving a postmortem stub in #postmortems. Tagging @oncall: we should verify there are no other tenants affected by the same sync run.

sofia: copying support ticket link: https://support.redwood/acme/5319 — noting customer impact timeline and consent for emergency change.

quota-bot: [automated scan] detected 4 other tenants with window_unit == "" and last-sync within 24h. Created triage items.

mike: ok, assigning follow-up to eng-oncall + product. We'll do a coordinated mass-fix with communication. Closing thread once triage done.
